source.Name: Total population
source.Summary: Population: Total population and distribution by age and sex estimated to be  consistent with the population by age and sex of the (a) 1970, 1982, 2004,  2014 censuses; (b) adjusted censuses for underenumeration; (c) official  estimates through 1969; and with estimates of the subsequent trends in  fertility, mortality and international migration.Note: Estimated to be consistent with the coverage of the territory of Western  Sahara in successive censuses of Morocco.

source.Name: Total fertility rate
source.Summary: Fertility: Total fertility rate and age pattern of fertility based on: (a) births in  the household in the preceding 12 (or 24) months classified by age of  mother from the 1982, 1994, 2004 censuses and 2009-2010 END; (b) indirect  estimates obtained from the application of the reverse survival method to  the 1982, 1994, 2004 censuses.Note: Fertility estimates for several regions of Western Sahara  (Oued-Ed-Dahab-Lagouira and Laayoune-Boujdour-Sakia El Hamra), as reported  in successive censuses of Morocco.

source.Name: Life expectancy at birth
source.Summary: Overall Mortality: Life expectancy at birth and age pattern of mortality based on: (a) In the  absence of statistics indicative of mortality levels and trends, mortality  was assumed to have levels similar to those estimated for neighbouring  countries with similar socio-economic conditions; (b) estimates of  under-five mortality (5q0) by assuming that the age pattern of mortality  conforms to the CD West model life tables.

source.Name: Infant/child mortality
source.Summary: Child Mortality: Under-five mortality based on: In the absence of statistics indicative of  mortality levels and trends, mortality was assumed to have levels similar  to those estimated for neighbouring countries with similar socio-economic  conditions.

source.Name: International migration
source.Summary: Migration: International migration based on: (a) information on foreign-born  populations from censuses and registers from major countries of  destination; (b) estimates derived as the differences between overall  population growth and natural increase; (c) UNHCR statistics on the number  of refugees in the main countries of asylum.
